youtube.title: Why Basketballs Are Covered in Bumps 🏀 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
A basketball's surface is covered in small raised bumps called pebbling. A smooth ball turns slippery when fingertips sweat. The pebbles bite into skin, and the grooves between them give moisture somewhere to go, so players keep control while dribbling and shooting.

Subscribe to The Hidden Why for a new why every day.
